subject: frustrating problems with ggplot2 - identical script works one day,  not the next.

messages.author: 0ec80bca575e544b
messages.subject: frustrating problems with ggplot2 - identical script works one day,  not the next.
parts:
Hello

I have been using ggplot2 for the last three months and find it
amazing. However I'm having some problems that I can't seem to find
the solution for.

Essentially half the time I start up R (in Mac) and attempt to use
ggplot, I get the following error message when plotting using wither
ggplot or qplot:

"Error in rename.default(x, .base_to_ggplot) : object '.data' not
found"

All my work is script based, and I know my scripts have worked in the
past. However, I will have to restart R multiple time (and sometimes
the computer) before I can manage to get ggplot to work again. My gut
feeling is that this issue is related to previously restored work
spaces, but I for the life of my can't figure out a correction.

If anyone has any ideas what may be causing this problem, I would love
to hear from you.

Thanks for your time,

David Roth

messages.author: 3b0940ce7a895cd1
messages.subject: Re: frustrating problems with ggplot2 - identical script works one  day, not the next.
parts:
This is not the shared experience with ggplot, which for most of us has proved highly reliable.
The experience you are reporting is more consistent with memory leaks, a poor install (I had something similar once), or
some other site-specific anomaly.

I'd uninstall R, remove all the libraries and start from square 1. It should only take a few minutes to do this, and perhaps it
will resolve your performance issues.

messages.author: 0ec80bca575e544b
messages.subject: Re: frustrating problems with ggplot2 - identical script works one  day, not the next.
parts:
To anyone who is interested, I think I found a solution to the problem
stated above. As Hadey suggested, it looks to be an issue with
previously saved workspaces. This solution is for the Mac version of R
(and the problem may be unique to the mac version as well).

I used the following commands in the terminal, and have had no
problems since.

mv ~/.RData ~/workspace.RData
mv ~/.Rhistory ~/history.txt


Dave Roth
